title: May and might
summary: **May** и **might** для возможности в настоящем и прошлом (**may/might have + V3**), уступки («может, и дорого, но...»), **may/might as well, may well**, упрёка **You might have told me!** и формального разрешения.
ru:
## Возможность: may и might
В значении «возможно» **may** и **might** во многом взаимозаменяемы. **May** слегка уверенней, **might** — осторожней и чуть менее вероятно; в разговорной речи разница минимальна:
> I **may** go to the conference, or I **might** stay at home. — Может быть, поеду на конференцию, а может, останусь дома.
> It **might** snow tonight. — Возможно, ночью пойдёт снег.
Отрицание: **may not / might not** («возможно, не»). Помните: **can't** значит «невозможно», а **may not** — «возможно, нет»:
> She **may not** know. — Возможно, она не знает.
> She **can't** know. — Она не может знать. (я уверен)
В вопросах о возможности may не используют: ~~May it be true?~~ → **Could** it be true? / Is it possible that it's true?

## Возможность в прошлом: may/might have + V3
> She **may have** missed the train. — Возможно, она опоздала на поезд.
> I **might have been** dreaming, but I thought I heard footsteps. — Может, мне и приснилось, но мне показалось, что я слышал шаги.
С **might have** есть второе значение — **нереализованная возможность** (только **might**, не may):
> You **might have been** killed! — Тебя могли убить! (но не убили)

## May well, might well, may as well
- **may / might well** — «вполне вероятно»: She **may well** win. — Она вполне может победить.
- **may / might as well** — «можно и..., всё равно делать нечего»: There's nothing on TV, so we **might as well** go to bed. — По телевизору ничего нет, так что можно и лечь.

## Уступка и упрёк
- **Уступка** («хотя и»): It **may** be expensive, but it's worth every penny. — Пусть дорого, зато стоит каждой копейки. Try as I **might**, I couldn't open the lid. — Как я ни старался, открыть крышку не смог.
- **Упрёк** (раздражение, обычно с might have): You **might have** told me you were leaving! — Мог бы и сказать, что уходишь! You **might** at least say thank you. — Мог бы хотя бы сказать спасибо.

## Разрешение и формальный стиль
- **May I...?** — формально-вежливо; **Might I...?** — очень формально, осторожно: **Might I** ask who is calling? — Позвольте спросить, кто звонит?
- Запрет в правилах: Students **may not** use dictionaries. — Студентам не разрешается пользоваться словарями.
- В косвенной речи **might** — прошедшая форма от may: She said she **might** come. — Она сказала, что, возможно, придёт.
- Мягкий совет: You **might want to** check the settings. — Вам, может быть, стоит проверить настройки.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~May it be true?~~ → **Could** it be true?
- ~~He may to come.~~ → He **may come**.
- ~~She might has left.~~ → She **might have left**.
- ~~Can she be late?~~ (как предположение) → **Could** she be late?
en:
## Possibility: may and might
In the meaning 'perhaps' **may** and **might** are often interchangeable. **May** is slightly more confident, **might** a little more tentative; in speech the difference is small:
> I **may** go to the conference, or I **might** stay at home.
> It **might** snow tonight.
Negative: **may not / might not** ('perhaps not'). **Can't** means 'impossible', while **may not** means 'perhaps not':
> She **may not** know.
> She **can't** know. (I am sure)
We do not use may in questions about possibility: ~~May it be true?~~ → **Could** it be true?

## Past possibility: may/might have + past participle
> She **may have** missed the train.
> I **might have been** dreaming, but I thought I heard footsteps.
**Might have** (not may) also shows an **unrealised possibility**:
> You **might have been** killed! (but you weren't)

## May well, might well, may as well
- **may / might well** — quite likely: She **may well** win.
- **may / might as well** — there is no reason not to: There's nothing on TV, so we **might as well** go to bed.

## Concession and reproach
- **Concession**: It **may** be expensive, but it's worth every penny. Try as I **might**, I couldn't open the lid.
- **Reproach** (irritation, usually might have): You **might have** told me you were leaving! You **might** at least say thank you.

## Permission and formal style
- **May I ...?** is formal and polite; **Might I ...?** is very formal: **Might I** ask who is calling?
- Rules: Students **may not** use dictionaries.
- In reported speech **might** is the past of may: She said she **might** come.
- Soft advice: You **might want to** check the settings.

## Common mistakes
- ~~May it be true?~~ → **Could** it be true?
- ~~He may to come.~~ → He **may come**.
- ~~She might has left.~~ → She **might have left**.
structure:
## Формулы
| Значение | Форма | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| возможно, сейчас/позже | may / might + V | She **may** know. |
| возможно, прошлое | may / might have + V3 | He **might have** left. |
| возможно, в процессе | may / might have been + V-ing | They **may have been** waiting. |
| вполне вероятно | may / might well + V | He **may well** resign. |
| можно и... | may / might as well + V | We **might as well** go. |
| нереализованная возможность | might have + V3 | You **might have** fallen. |
| упрёк | might (at least) / might have + V3 | You **might have** called. |
| формальная просьба | May / Might I + V? | **May** I come in? |

## Сравнение: may not, can't, couldn't
| Форма | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| may not / might not | возможно, нет | She **may not** be home. |
| can't | невозможно, уверен | She **can't** be home. |
| may not (правило) | не разрешается | You **may not** park here. |

## Отрицание и вопрос
> He **may not** / **might not** come. — **mightn't** редко, **mayn't** устарело.
> **May** I ...? — **Yes, you may.** / No, you **may not**.
> Возможность в вопросе: **Could** / **Might** she be ill? (не May)

exercises.title: May / might
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужную форму: may, might (иногда с have, well или as well). Допустимые варианты засчитываются.

items.text: I haven't decided yet. I {{may|might|could}} go to the conference, or I {{may|might|could}} stay at home.
It {{may not|might not}} be cheap, but it's worth every penny.
She {{may well|might well}} win; she has trained harder than anyone.
There's nothing on TV, so we {{may as well|might as well}} go to bed.
He {{might have|may have}} missed the train; he's very late.
You {{might have|could have}} told me you were bringing guests!
{{May|Might}} I ask what you are doing here?

exercises.title: Подберите форму
exercises.instruction: Вставьте подходящее слово. Допустимые варианты засчитываются.

items.text: She said she {{might|may}} come, but she hasn't confirmed yet.
You {{might|could}} at least have said thank you.
Try as I {{might|may}}, I couldn't open the lid.
I can't find my keys. I {{may|might}} have left them in the car.
It {{could|might|may}} rain later, so take an umbrella.
Students {{may not|must not|mustn't}} use dictionaries during the exam.

items.q: I'm not sure where Anna is. She ___ be at the gym.
He ___ well be the best candidate for the job.
You ___ have told me you were leaving! I was worried sick.
There's no point waiting here. We ___ go home.
She ___ have heard the news; I'm not sure.
'___ I borrow your laptop?' 'Yes, of course you may.'

items.why: В косвенной речи **might** — прошедшая форма от may.
**might have + V3** в раздражённом тоне — «мог бы и позвонить».

items.q: Какой вопрос о возможности построен неверно?
options: Is it possible that it's true?
items.why: В вопросах о возможности may не используется.

options: Можно и подождать — всё равно делать нечего.

items.q: 'He might have been killed in that crash' (но он остался жив) означает:
options: Он мог погибнуть, но не погиб.
Might I ask who is calling?
Can I ask who is calling?

exercises.title: Перепишите с may / might
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя слово или конструкцию в скобках.

items.prompt: Perhaps she will accept the offer. (may) → She ...
It is possible that he missed the train. (might have) → He ...
answers: He might have missed the train.

items.prompt: It's quite likely that they will cancel the event. (may well) → They ...
answers: They may well cancel the event.
They might well cancel the event.

items.prompt: There's nothing better to do, so let's stay in. (might as well) → We ...
answers: We might as well stay in.
We may as well stay in.

items.prompt: I'm angry that you didn't tell me. (might have, reproach) → You ... (tell)
Although the hotel is cheap, it is very clean. (may) → The hotel ...
answers: The hotel may be cheap, but it is very clean.
The hotel may be cheap, but it's very clean.
The hotel may be cheap but it is very clean.
The hotel may be cheap but it's very clean.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя may или might.

items.prompt: What might you do next weekend?
items.sample: I might visit my parents or I might go hiking.

items.prompt: Write about something that may happen in your country in the next few years.
items.sample: Electric cars may become much cheaper in the next few years.

items.prompt: Explain why a friend didn't call you (may have / might have).
items.sample: She may have forgotten her phone at home.

items.prompt: Write a sentence with a concession: 'It may be ..., but ...'.
items.sample: It may be a small flat, but it's very bright and quiet.

items.prompt: Write about a danger you narrowly avoided (might have).
items.sample: I might have missed my flight if the taxi had been five minutes later.

items.prompt: What might happen if you don't sleep enough?
items.sample: I might make mistakes at work, and I may even get ill.
